passage_text:
Researchers studied the effect of a novel antihypertensive drug on systolic blood pressure (SBP) in 12 patients with stage‑1 hypertension. Each patient’s baseline SBP was measured, then the drug was administered at a fixed dose of 10 mg once daily for four weeks. After the treatment period, SBP was measured again. The study aimed to determine the drug’s efficacy and identify any patient‑specific predictors of response. The investigators recorded the following data:

- Patient ID
- Baseline SBP (mmHg)
- Post‑treatment SBP (mmHg)
- Age (years)

The table below summarizes the results for the 12 participants. The researchers plan to perform a paired t‑test to assess the significance of the SBP change and to explore correlations with age.
stem: Which patient experienced the greatest absolute reduction in systolic blood pressure after the four‑week treatment?
explanation: Correct: D) P03 fell from 158 to 140 mmHg, a reduction of 18 mmHg, the largest. Why the others are wrong: A) P01 fell 15 mmHg. B) P07 fell 15 mmHg despite having the highest baseline (160). C) P12 fell 14 mmHg.
trap: Choosing P07 because it has the highest baseline SBP, when its reduction (15 mmHg) is smaller than P03's 18 mmHg.

stem: Which study design would best allow the researchers to attribute changes in SBP to the drug rather than to confounding variables?

options.A: Randomized controlled trial with a placebo arm
options.B: Prospective cohort study of patients receiving the drug
options.C: Case‑control study comparing patients who responded versus did not respond
options.D: Cross‑sectional survey of patients’ BP before and after drug use

explanation: A randomized controlled trial (RCT) with a placebo arm controls for both known and unknown confounders, allowing causal inference about the drug’s effect on SBP.
trap: Students may incorrectly select the cohort design because it also involves prospective data collection, but it lacks randomization.

stem: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the data presented in the passage?

options.A: Every patient's SBP was lower after treatment than at baseline.
options.B: The drug lowered SBP more than a placebo would have.
options.C: The reduction in SBP varied among patients.
options.D: The study used a fixed drug dose for all participants.

explanation: Correct: B) All 12 patients received the drug and there was no placebo or comparison group, so a drug-versus-placebo claim cannot be made. Why the others are wrong: A) Every reduction in the table is positive (13 to 18 mmHg). C) Reductions ranged from 13 to 18 mmHg. D) The passage states 10 mg once daily for all.
trap: Reading a before-and-after drop as proof the drug outperformed placebo when no control group exists.
